name: Kunta Kinteh Island and Related Sites
description: Kunta Kinteh Island sits in the Gambia River about 30 km from the sea, where the crumbling ruins of Fort James still stand. For centuries European powers used the fort to trade in goods and enslaved people. Nearby, the riverbank village of Albreda has a ruined Portuguese chapel and a colonial warehouse, while Fort Bullen guards the river mouth, together telling the story of the slave trade and its end.
